EXPECTED: the typed height (8000 m) puts the vessel there, same tolerance.

EXPECTED: an offset of 5400 s (a quarter of Kerbin's day) moves the game's clock by 5400 s plus the game's physics time between the readings (Time.fixedTime: the game's clock falls behind the real time at a low frame rate), within 2 s.
EXPECTED: an offset of -5400 s moves it back by 10800 s (plus the physics time), within 2 s.
INFORMATION: the sun's elevation over the vessel before the time controls.
INFORMATION: the larger change of the sun's elevation over the two offsets.
EXPECTED: the sun's elevation changes by more than 3 degrees for at least one of the two offsets (a quarter day each way). Fails: the sun does not follow the clock.
EXPECTED: Freeze Time holds the game's clock within 0.25 s over 3 s while the viewer's natural time runs on by the game's physics time (2 s).
INFORMATION: the viewer's natural time (the game's clock advance while the time is held) per second of the game's physics time over the 3 s freeze; about 1.

EXPECTED: that ratio is 0.85 to 1.15. It proves the reference the time rows and restore_time use (Time.fixedTime) is the one the game's clock follows. Fails: the game's clock advances differently from its physics time; then the time rows' reference has to change.

EXPECTED: after the freeze the clock runs on from where it was held: held UT plus the physics time since, within 2 s, and the clock must have advanced by at least half the physics time since the resume (a stopped clock cannot pass at a low frame rate).
